last_outcome: M1-12 done (iteration 22): packages/flight-sim/src/project.ts's projectSegments(segments, viewport, paddingRatio) turns arcSegments()'s antimeridian-split lat/lon output into one {x,y} array per segment, sharing a single scale on both axes and centering the fit so the constraining axis touches paddingRatio*viewport exactly. The real difficulty was reconstructing a true bounding box across split segments without a second unsplit-path parameter: unwrapLongitudes walks every segment in order without resetting 'previous longitude' at a segment boundary, and accumulates a running +-360 offset whenever a jump exceeds 180 -- which by splitAtAntimeridian's own guarantee can only happen at a segment boundary, never inside one. Self-review (/code-review --effort high) found a real gap beyond the three listed acceptance criteria: paddingRatio was trusted verbatim, so >= 0.5 (e.g. a caller passing a percentage like 50 meaning '50%') drove scale negative and silently mirrored every point, and exactly 0.5 collapsed the whole route to a single point -- fixed by clamping to [0, 0.49], matching geo.ts's own interpolate's existing clamp-rather-than-throw precedent for its f parameter. No supabase/, auth or RLS touched, so no /security-review per LOOP.md section 4. pnpm run verify green throughout; gate:tests floor raised 167 -> 168 (+5: three acceptance-criteria tests, an empty-input test, and the padding-ratio-clamp regression test); gate:roadmap unchanged at 20 done/9 pending (M1-05's split already accounted for this item on the roadmap).
